props.gloss_en: Beit Shammai: one wipes his hands with the towel and sets it on the table
Beit Shammai: for if you say on the cushion -- a decree lest the liquids in the towel become impure through the cushion and in turn defile the hands
a vessel does not defile a vessel
a vessel does not defile a person
Beit Hillel: for if you say on the table -- a decree lest the liquids in the towel become impure through the table and in turn defile the food
Beit Hillel, another reason: there is no washing of the hands for non-sacred food from the Torah
here we deal with a second[-degree] table
and a second does not make a third in non-sacred food except through liquids
Beit Shammai hold it is forbidden to use a second[-degree] table
Beit Shammai: a decree because of those who eat teruma
Beit Hillel hold it is permitted to use a second[-degree] table
Beit Hillel: those who eat teruma are careful
better that hands be defiled, which have no root in Torah law, and not food, which has a root in Torah law

objections.gloss_en: ונטמייה כסת למפה! -- let the cushion defile the towel [directly]; why speak of the liquids in it?

answered_by.gloss_en: אין כלי מטמא כלי -- a vessel does not defile a vessel (= p_ein_kli_metamei_kli)

objections.gloss_en: ונטמייה כסת לגברא גופיה! -- let the cushion defile the man himself

answered_by.gloss_en: אין כלי מטמא אדם -- a vessel does not defile a person (= p_ein_kli_metamei_adam)

objections.gloss_en: ולטמא שלחן לאוכלין שבתוכו! -- let the table defile the food on it [directly]; why speak of the liquids in the towel?
